about: Investigations: experiments that set up the main experiments' configuration, grouped by what they study. `group` is mechanistic (model-level measurements, no editing method: `scope: model`, their own page), sweep (per-method hyperparameter sweeps on dev records; each lists the methods that have the setting, under the name their hparams file uses), or input (whether what the model is given changes a result: how the prompt is written, and what context is added to it; `scope` still decides whether one is per model or a per-method sweep). `datasets: all` makes a sweep start with every runnable dataset that has dev records selected, less any path containing an entry of `datasets_except` (subsets that repeat another's records); a sweep spec can ask for that set with data_paths ["default"]. `status: planned` lists an investigation that is not built yet. For sweeps, `kind` decides the suggested values: log (multiply the default by factors), int (scale the default), layer (one layer), layer_window (a contiguous block of the default's width), layer_span (every layer, a half or a quarter of the model, or a window around its traced peak), choice (listed options), bool. `stability` is how the authors' default varies: robust (same everywhere), model, data, not_reported. Sweeps run on dev records only.

investigations.label: Knowledge localisation
investigations.question: Where in each model is a fact recalled, and how reliably is it in early-to-mid MLP layers? Causal tracing, per model: no editing method is involved.

investigations.label: Neuron attribution
investigations.question: Which individual MLP neurons carry a fact, and does switching them off take it away? Integrated-gradient attribution per neuron (the unit Knowledge Neurons, FiNE and NMKE edit), tested against random neurons and on other facts.

investigations.label: Circuit tracing
investigations.question: Which attention heads, MLPs and paths between them carry a fact from the subject to the answer, and is that circuit enough on facts it was not chosen from? The circuit-level unit that circuit-aware editors target.

investigations.label: Edit layers
investigations.question: Which layer, or block of layers, should each method write its edit into, starting from the model's traced peak?

scanning_ceiling.note: WilKE picks a layer per fact from 0..scanning_ceiling; this bounds the search

top_k.note: FiDAL picks this many layers per fact by Fisher information

investigations.cost_note: Each new layer for MEMIT, PMET, AlphaEdit, NMKE, WilKE and FiDAL needs covariance statistics computed once per model: 6 to 12 minutes and up to 1 GB per layer.

investigations.label: Neurons and masks
investigations.question: How many neurons may the edit touch, and how strict is the selection?

neuron_num.note: more neurons help generalizability and hurt locality

p.note: share of paraphrases a neuron must appear in (with refine)

investigations.label: Adapter placement and rank
investigations.question: Which modules get adapters, and how much capacity do they have?

investigations.label: Weight-update strength
investigations.question: How hard do methods that train weights directly push the update?

lr_scale.note: the original code and EasyEdit disagree on the erase and write strengths

investigations.label: Value-vector optimisation
investigations.question: How hard do locate-and-edit methods optimise the target vector they write?

investigations.label: Preservation strength
investigations.question: How strongly is existing knowledge protected while the edit is written?

investigations.label: Covariance statistics
investigations.question: How many samples estimate the key covariance that protects preserved knowledge?
investigations.cost_note: Every new sample count recomputes the statistics for each edited layer.

investigations.label: Fine-tuning (FT)
investigations.question: How should plain fine-tuning be set up: its loss (FT-M on the whole target, or FT-L at the last prompt token), which layer it trains, how hard and how long, and how it is held near the original weights?

objective_optimization.note: target_new is FT-M: cross-entropy on every target token after the prompt (EasyEdit's recommended FT). prompt_last is FT-L, the ROME paper's constrained fine-tuning: the target scored at the last prompt position. Hold it fixed to tune FT-M and FT-L separately, or sweep both to compare them

weight_decay.note: Adam's L2 term pulls the edited weights toward zero, not toward the original weights; norm_constraint is what keeps them near the originals

investigations.label: LoRA
investigations.question: How should LoRA be set up: where the adapters go and how big they are, how hard and how long they train, and how they are regularised?

layers.note: which layers get adapters: [] (shown as all) is every layer, the current setting; the others are a half or a quarter of the model, or a window around its traced peak

weight_decay.note: decays the adapter toward zero, which is toward the original model

lora_type.note: AdaLoRA prunes the adapter's rank over the run. gpt-j-6b's hparams file uses it; every other model uses plain LoRA

investigations.label: SCR (Selective Contextual Reasoning)
investigations.question: Which parts of retrieve, confirm, answer make SCR work: the retriever and how many facts it returns, whether and how strictly facts are confirmed, and how they are put in front of the model? Run across as many datasets as possible, since retrieval difficulty depends on the data.

retrieval_k.note: about 5 for Wiki data, 1 to 3 for ZsRE in the paper

sentence_model_name.note: the retriever's embedding model; others download from Hugging Face on first use

min_similarity.note: cosine-similarity floor for a retrieved fact; null is no floor (always retrieval_k facts)

kb_key.note: what a fact is found by: the edit sentence, or its subject alone (the sentence when a record has no subject)

latest_edit_wins.note: a new edit of the same prompt replaces the older one in the knowledge base

confirm.note: off keeps every retrieved fact: plain retrieve-and-answer, the ablation of what confirmation adds

confirm_margin.note: a fact passes when the Yes logit beats No by more than this; higher trades generalisation for locality

confirm_shots.note: worked Yes/No examples (about invented places) before the confirmation question

max_confirmed.note: most facts that reach the answer, the most confident first; 0 is no cap

fact_order.note: most_similar_last puts the best match next to the question

answer_template.note: instructed adds: Use the facts above to answer the question when they apply

no_context_framing.note: how a question is asked when no fact is confirmed: bare (the query alone, as originally) or framed (Question/Answer, the same as with facts, so the format does not depend on confirmation)

investigations.label: IKE demonstrations
investigations.question: How many demonstrations does IKE put in the prompt? (SCR has its own investigation.)

k.note: demonstrations per query; 32 in the original paper, 16 in EasyEdit

investigations.label: Knowledge by prompt format
investigations.question: In which prompt formats do base and instruct models show what they know? The same facts from each dataset asked as completions, questions, through the chat template, as multiple choice and as riddles.

investigations.label: Where facts are recalled, by format
investigations.question: Does the prompt's format move where a model recalls a fact? Causal tracing of the same facts in each format.
